decision.rationale: PRR-019 is resolved: one total deadline now bounds serialization, lock waiting, startup and readiness, pre-write dispatch, and response waiting. Both pre-dispatch expiration paths write zero frames and preserve a healthy worker, post-dispatch mutating actions remain non-replayable, and all required local and exact-head CI gates pass.

summary: The three-commit delta records, fixes, and verifies PRR-019. Bounded lock acquisition plus deadline checks after lock acquisition and startup prevent expired actions from being written, while real subprocess tests prove zero writes and same-process recovery. No open blocking finding remains for the reviewed snapshot.

change_map.change: Serialize the request first and acquire the worker lock only within the remaining request budget.
change_map.external_behavior: A queued request returns timeout without late dispatch.
change_map.validation: The call completes while the lock remains held, records zero worker frames, and preserves the process.

change_map.change: Check the same deadline after worker startup and readiness immediately before stdin dispatch.
change_map.external_behavior: A ready worker is preserved if startup completion consumes the request budget.
change_map.validation: Delayed startup completion records zero frames and the follow-up request reuses the same process.

change_map.change: Retain worker termination on post-dispatch timeout and no one-shot action fallback or replay.
change_map.external_behavior: Unknown action outcomes are not automatically duplicated.
change_map.validation: The existing dispatched-action timeout test records one request and zero fallback runner calls.

change_map.change: Retain the readiness handshake, fd-level newline framing, and pipe cleanup.
change_map.external_behavior: Immediate responses remain ordered and worker resources close cleanly.
change_map.validation: One hundred query and action responses and ResourceWarning-as-error tests pass.

change_map.change: Keep public API, protocol schema, configuration, dependency, and version surfaces unchanged.
change_map.external_behavior: Existing 0.2.0 consumers retain the same public contract.
change_map.validation: Root and package suites, compile, preflight, wheel checks, and exact-head CI pass.

findings.title: Expired queued actions were dispatched before timeout was reported
findings.observation: The previous worker could exhaust its deadline waiting for the lock and still write. The current implementation serializes within the budget, bounds lock acquisition by remaining time, checks after acquisition, and checks again after startup and readiness immediately before writing.
findings.trigger: Another request holds the shared worker lock beyond this request timeout, or a restart reaches valid readiness but startup completion returns after the same deadline.
findings.impact: Before remediation, a mutating Accessibility action could begin after its caller timeout and then be retried as an unknown result. Both repaired paths now return timeout before dispatch and preserve a healthy process.

evidence.description: One monotonic deadline covers request serialization, bounded lock acquisition, startup and readiness, the final pre-write gate, and response waiting.
The lock-contention test completes while the lock remains held, records zero frames, and proves a follow-up uses the same process.
The delayed-startup test passes valid readiness, expires before write, records zero frames, and proves same-process follow-up.
The existing post-dispatch action timeout regression still records one dispatch and makes zero one-shot fallback calls.
Exact reviewed-head GitHub Actions completed successfully.

findings.remediation: Completed: bound worker access by the remaining request budget, check the deadline after lock acquisition and startup or readiness, return timeout with zero writes before dispatch, and preserve a healthy worker.
findings.verification: Completed: both zero-write counterexamples, same-process follow-up, framing stress, post-dispatch no-replay, package and root tests, compile, preflight, wheel checks, and exact-head CI passed.

required_actions.action: Prevent worker dispatch after queue or startup consumes the request deadline, preserve a healthy worker, and add deterministic zero-write regressions.

assumptions: A request timeout is a total caller budget including serialization, queue, startup and readiness, dispatch, and response time.
A mutating request is potentially dispatched once write and flush begin, so an unknown post-dispatch result must never trigger automatic replay.
Direct users may share one client across threads and the worker lock is the intended serialization boundary.
The existing three strict-mypy errors are outside this delta and are not a configured CI merge gate.
